newsitem.title: USA: Indianapolis Mayor unveils $437.9 mln FY 98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Indianapolis Mayor unveils $437.9 mln FY 98 budget.

text.p: Indianapolis Mayor Stephen Goldsmith announced a $437.9 million budget for fiscal 1998 with about $80 million for capital improvements.

Goldsmith's proposed budget presented to the Indianapolis City-County Council Monday night includes a slight increase over the current year attributable to more investment in police and fire services, Deputy Mayor Skip Stitt said.

Indianapolis projects spending slightly less than $80 million for infrastructure improvements in the fiscal year, which runs along the calendar year, and officials have not decided what percentage will be financed with cash and how much with debt, Stitt said.

The budget reflects the city's overall plan adopted two months ago to pay off $140 million of lease revenue bonds issued for the United Airlines maintenance facility, funding of police and fire pensions and anticipated expenses for sewer mandates, Stitt said.

The budget plan includes a small and "prudent" property tax rate reduction based on projected fund balances of more than $100 million, healthy growth in new home construction and new business startups, Stitt said.
Debt service as a percentage of the property tax rate, has decreased for six consecutive years and is projected to drop in fiscal 1998 as well, Stitt said.
Indianapolis has about $910.5 million of outstanding debt, city figures show.
The city-county council plans a number of hearings on the fiscal 1998 budget and is expected to approve it in a few weeks, Stitt said.
